source.title: BiomedGPT: A Unified and Generalist Biomedical Generative Pre-trained Transformer for Vision, Language, and Multimodal Tasks
source.authors: Kai Zhang; Jun Yu; Zhiling Yan; Yixin Liu; Eashan Adhikarla; S. Fu; Xun Chen; Chen Chen; Yuyin Zhou; Xiang Li; Li-Fang He; Brian D. Davison; Quan-Zheng Li; Yong Chen; Hongfang Liu; Li-Chao Sun

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies BiomedGPT model size and reports downstream task performance, which bears on V6, but it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or test a loss-scaling law.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream performance for several BiomedGPT sizes, including comparisons that bear on V6. It does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy, power-law fits, extrapolation from smaller runs, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. It also does not test architectural variation at fixed parameter count. Comparisons to prior systems are not extracted as rows unless they provide an explicit model-size result for BiomedGPT. Captioning scale values in Fig. 3b are omitted because the supplied flattened layout does not reliably associate every number with its model and metric.
record.test_reason: The study trains three BiomedGPT sizes (33M, 93M, 182M) and reports fine-tuned downstream scores for each across many biomedical vision-language tasks. This bears on V6 (downstream performance improves with scale) in a new setting. It is a weak test: three points within less than one order of magnitude, and no fitted or predictive curve. It reports no pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim a 'direct correlation between increased model scale and enhanced performance', for both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings. They also note saturation on several datasets such as SZ-CXR, more pronounced at very low image resolution. They do not claim or test a predictive law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a biomedical multimodal model-scale evaluation, not a reproduction of the original language-model held-out-loss scaling measurements; it compares three fine-tuned model sizes on downstream tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scale trend varies by dataset: the paper notes saturation on several datasets, and the MedMNIST-Raw table includes a retinal OCT decrease from medium to base and no increase from medium to base on breast ultrasound.
record.problems: The study evaluates only three BiomedGPT sizes (33M, 93M, and 182M) for these comparisons, reports no uncertainty for the extracted scale rows, and does not fit predictive scaling curves or test prediction from smaller runs. Some other scale-comparison values in the supplied flattened figure text cannot be assigned reliably.
record.rows_left_out: Captioning scale metrics from Fig. 3b were left out because the supplied flattened table layout did not reliably assign all values to model, dataset, and metric. Other scale-related plotted results were not extracted where the text did not provide model-specific values. No rows were omitted due to the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Predictability: no curve fitted, no extrapolation, and no prediction from pretraining loss. Only three sizes spanning about 5.5x in parameters, far short of several orders of magnitude.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Multimodal, but no loss power law is fitted.

missing.what: Captioning scores by size are readable. IU X-ray CIDEr 29.6/31.3/40.1. PEIR GROSS ROUGE-L 25.8/24.0/36.0 (medium below small) and CIDEr 22.0/25.8/122.7. MIMIC-CXR CIDEr 12.8/12.9/23.4. METEOR and ROUGE-L are also given for each dataset.
In-hospital mortality accuracy S/M/B: 77.8/89.2/89.5 (saturation between M and B).
Treatment suggestion (B 50.0±5.3) and clinical trial matching (B 85.2±1.5 vs 75.4 and 71.6) scores for the three sizes. Zero-shot VQA-RAD accuracy for BiomedGPT and Instruct-BiomedGPT S/M/B.
Coronal Abdominal CT 92.2/92.3/93.1 (nearly flat) and Sagittal Abdominal CT 80.0/82.0/82.3. Not extracted.
RadGPT S/M/B transfer results. On liver CT, scaling up was needed to match a ResNet-50 baseline.

record.verdict_notes: Size is confounded with fine-tuning setup. For image classification and VQA, base uses 384×384 inputs while medium and small use 256×256, and batch size differs by size (Supplementary Table 5). Part of the base model's gain may therefore come from resolution, not parameters. All sizes are initialised from OFA checkpoints of matching size. No uncertainty is given for the size comparisons except the cross-validated tasks.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relation in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No predictions from small runs are compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling is tested.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
The paper evaluates biomedical and multimodal tasks, but does not test whether the same pretraining-loss power law holds in other modalities or regimes.

The study compares downstream task metrics across a few model sizes; it does not fit predictive scaling curves, test prediction from pretraining loss, or establish predictability over several orders of magnitude.
No sensitivity analysis of scaling-law fitting choices or systematic test for curvature in a loss-scaling curve.

relationships.condition: Most fine-tuned tasks: VQA (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA open-ended), MC-CXR, low-res MedMNIST chest X-ray and blood cell; 33M→182M
relationships.reason: Scores rise monotonically with size, often by large margins (e.g., vqa-rad-oe 13.4→53.6→60.9; mc-cxr 75.9→82.8→89.7). Rows vqa-rad-*, slake-*, pathvqa-oe-*, mc-cxr-*, chest-*, blood-*.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased monotonically with size, including VQA-RAD open-ended scores of 13.4, 53.6, and 60.9 and MC-CXR scores of 75.9, 82.8, and 89.7.

relationships.condition: Low-res MedMNIST retinal OCT, breast ultrasound, colon, dermatoscopy, abdominal CT; PathVQA closed-ended; SZ-CXR
relationships.reason: Gains are small, flat or non-monotonic: OCT base 81.6 is below medium 81.9; ultrasound medium equals base at 87.8. Colon, derma, CT and PathVQA closed-ended gain only about 1.5–3 points. The authors report saturation on SZ-CXR and at very small image resolutions. Rows oct-*, us-*, colon-*, derma-*, ct-*, pathvqa-ce-*.
relationships.display_finding: OCT base scored 81.6 versus medium's 81.9, ultrasound variants tied at 87.8, several tasks gained only about 1.5–3 points, and SZ-CXR and very low-resolution tasks saturated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Model-size comparisons on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, colon pathology, dermatoscopy, chest X-ray, blood-cell microscopy, coronal abdominal CT, and MC-CXR
reader_labels.reason: The larger checkpoints generally have higher downstream scores than the small checkpoint; see the paired size comparisons in rows vqa-rad-ce-m, vqa-rad-ce-b, vqa-rad-oe-m, vqa-rad-oe-b, slake-ce-m, slake-ce-b, slake-oe-m, slake-oe-b, pathvqa-ce-m, pathvqa-ce-b, pathvqa-oe-m, pathvqa-oe-b, colon-m, colon-b, derma-m, derma-b, chest-m, chest-b, blood-m, blood-b, ct-m, ct-b, mc-cxr-m, and mc-cxr-b.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Retinal OCT and breast ultrasound MedMNIST-Raw results
reader_labels.reason: The larger-size results are not strictly increasing: base retinal OCT accuracy is below medium, and base breast-ultrasound accuracy equals medium; see rows oct-m, oct-b, us-m, and us-b. The study also does not fit or validate a prediction rule.
